added_lemmas.justification: The certified ray proves balanced allocation for every privacy budget at least 1000, while the pointwise bracket and two-sided interval exclusion rule out a universal balanced-binary channel story.
added_lemmas.gap: Kairouz, Oh, and Viswanath and Ghazi, Nasser, Calmon, and Issa prove binary or partition structure for single-draw divergence objectives, not this fourfold composite-confidence loss or its allocation game.
added_lemmas.consumer: At these four-unit parameters, a protocol designer may restrict the allocation to two treated units for every privacy budget at least 1000, but must retain nonbinary channel candidates near 1000.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The round-2 directive makes the old pointwise allocation clause obsolete; inbound dependencies should migrate to the proved replacement theorem containing the uniform balance ray while preserving the pointwise bracket, exclusion interval, and nonconvexity witness.

prose_updates.tldr: Exact finite-population SATE inference under local privacy reduces to a fourteen-pattern, degree-\(N\) polynomial channel game with an inner exact confidence linear program. At \(N=4\), \(\alpha=2/5\), and \(\lambda=1000\), rational certificates bracket the unrestricted optimum within \(5.94\times10^{-6}\), while revealed-input dominance and monotone privacy feasibility force balanced allocation for every \(\lambda\ge1000\). Four-ary response strictly beats every balanced binary-partition response throughout \([999.9,1000.1]\). No optimizer-attaining balanced-binary cell or actual equality-set boundary is established.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The proved contribution consists of the exact orbit kernel, fourteen-output Blackwell refinement, fixed-channel primal--dual program, attained polynomial formulation, nonconvexity witness, global positive-tolerance bracket, balanced allocation for \(N=4\), \(\alpha=2/5\), and every \(\lambda\ge1000\), and the nonbinary exclusion interval \([999.9,1000.1]\). The certificate-characterization theorem remains conditional: it explains how an explicitly supplied attaining family would certify a cell and boundary, but no such family is supplied. In particular, the paper does not claim a nonempty balanced-binary equality cell, an endpoint polynomial, an isolated root, a sign-certified phase transition, four-output sufficiency, general-\(N\) balance, or a practical advantage at conventional coverage. Consumer use requires a hidden-assignment protocol in which the analyst observes only privatized reports and the known design quantities.
